summary: ZrO2 thin films were grown using novel cyclopentadienyl-type precursors (CpMe)2ZrMe2 and (CpMe)2Zr(OMe)Me with ozone as the oxygen source. The ALD process was verified at 350 /C14 C, where highly conformal films were deposited. The films were stoichiometric and polycrystalline, with the metastable cubic phase increasing with decreasing film thickness. The study aimed to explore the ALD process for ZrO2 films with improved thermal stability and uniformity.
evidence: ZrO2 thin ﬁlms were grown onto silicon (100) substrates by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using novel cyclopentadienyl-type precursors, namely (CpMe) 2ZrMe2 and (CpMe) 2Zr(OMe)Me (Cp ¼ cyclopentadienyl, C5H5) together with ozone as the oxygen source. Growth characteristics were studied in the temperature range of 250 to 500 /C14 C. An ALD-type self-limiting growth mode was verified for both processes at 350 /C14 C where highly conformal films were deposited onto high aspect ratio trenches. The films grown from both precursors were stoichiometric and polycrystalline with an increasing contribution from the metastable cubic phase with decreasing film thickness.
